# Rollout Plan: Migration of 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing System to New Billing System

## Overview

Both billing systems (legacy "BILL-OLD" and new "BILL-NEW") will run concurrently throughout the migration. Users are migrated in discrete batches; each user's billing records, payment methods, invoicing history, and active subscriptions must be verified in BILL-NEW before that user's billing-of-record is switched over. The legacy system remains fully operational as a fallback and system of record for unmigrated users through every phase below — it is not touched (no deletion, disabling, or decommissioning) until a dedicated post-migration phase that follows the final migration batch.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (2% of users, ~800 users)

**Entry criterion:** BILL-NEW has passed a full parallel-run reconciliation test against BILL-OLD for 30 consecutive days using synthetic/shadow traffic (0 unresolved discrepancies over $1), dual-write/dual-read architecture is confirmed working in staging, and rollback tooling (per-user revert to BILL-OLD as system of record) has been tested successfully in a dry run.

**Population:** Internal employee accounts and opted-in low-risk beta users (non-enterprise, monthly billing, no active disputes).

**Duration:** 2 weeks minimum before proceeding.

**Exit criterion to advance:** Metrics below within threshold for the full duration, and manual audit of 100% of pilot accounts' invoices confirms accuracy.

---

## Phase 2: Early Majority (25% of users, ~10,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 exit criteria met; billing discrepancy rate in Phase 1 was below 0.1% of transactions; support ticket volume attributable to billing migration in Phase 1 was below 2% of migrated users; engineering sign-off that all P0/P1 defects found in Phase 1 are resolved and deployed.

**Population:** Randomized sample stratified across plan types (excluding enterprise/custom-contract accounts), weighted toward monthly (not annual) billing cycles so a full billing cycle can be observed quickly.

**Duration:** 3–4 weeks, migrated in weekly sub-batches (e.g., ~2,500/week) to allow metric checkpoints between sub-batches.

**Exit criterion to advance:** Metrics within threshold across all weekly sub-batches; at least one full monthly billing cycle completed cleanly for the earliest sub-batch in this phase.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability / Full Migration (73% of users, remaining ~29,200 users, including annual and enterprise accounts)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 exit criteria met; enterprise/custom-contract test cohort (a small carve-out of ~50 representative enterprise accounts) has been migrated separately and successfully invoiced for one full cycle; customer support and finance teams have completed migration-specific training; customer communication/notice period (minimum 14 days' advance notice per contractual/legal requirements) has been sent to all remaining users.

**Population:** All remaining users, sequenced with enterprise/annual/custom-contract accounts migrated last within this phase (smaller final sub-batches, e.g., last 5% held for a dedicated final batch with extra manual review) given their higher revenue-per-account risk.

**Duration:** 4–6 weeks, in progressively sized sub-batches, with the final batch (highest-risk/enterprise accounts) migrated last and monitored for one full billing cycle before Phase 3 is declared complete.

**Exit criterion to advance:** All users successfully migrated and billed at least once through BILL-NEW; metrics within threshold; zero unresolved critical billing discrepancies.

---

## Phase 4 (Post-Migration, Separate from User Migration Phases): Legacy Decommission

**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 fully complete, including a minimum 60-day parallel-run retention window post-final-batch-migration during which BILL-OLD remains live, read-only, and available for reconciliation/audit/rollback reference; finance has completed a full close-the-books reconciliation between BILL-OLD and BILL-NEW; legal/compliance sign-off on data retention requirements.

**Action:** Only after this separate phase's entry criterion is met does decommissioning (disabling writes, archiving data, eventual shutdown) of BILL-OLD begin. This is explicitly not bundled with the final user-migration batch in Phase 3.

---

## Halt Metric

If, at any point during Phases 1–3, the **billing discrepancy rate exceeds 0.5% of transactions in any rolling 24-hour window**, the rollout is automatically halted: no further batches are migrated until root cause is identified and resolved, and previously migrated batches are not rolled back automatically but are placed under enhanced monitoring. Additional halt triggers: failed-payment rate for migrated users exceeding 1.5% above the BILL-OLD baseline, or customer-reported billing incidents exceeding 25 in a single day.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or missed charges during dual-write window due to sync race conditions | Implement idempotency keys on all transactions and a reconciliation job comparing BILL-OLD and BILL-NEW ledgers every 15 minutes with automated alerting on mismatch | Engineering Lead, Billing Platform
RISK: Enterprise customers with custom contract terms are misconfigured in BILL-NEW, causing incorrect invoicing | Migrate enterprise accounts last in a dedicated sub-batch with manual finance review and customer confirmation before cutover | Finance Operations Manager
RISK: Customer payment methods (stored cards/tokens) fail to migrate correctly, causing failed renewals | Run a payment-method validation pass (tokenized re-verification with the payment processor) prior to each batch and require successful validation before batch cutover | Payments Engineering Lead
RISK: Support team is overwhelmed by billing-related tickets during migration, delaying resolution and harming customer trust | Staff a dedicated migration support queue with escalation path and pre-written runbooks for known issue classes, staffed ahead of each phase | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Rollback for a migrated user is attempted after BILL-NEW has already generated a new invoice, causing double-billing on revert | Build and test a per-user rollback procedure that voids/cancels any BILL-NEW invoices as part of the revert transaction, verified in Phase 1 dry runs | Engineering Lead, Billing Platform

PHASES: 4
